title: Expansion machine simulation
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $x$ and $w$ be Boolean words, let $i$ be one of $k$ work tapes, let $\mathrm{pat}$ be a Boolean word, and let $c$ be a configuration of a $k$-tape Boolean machine whose state is $0$. Suppose a tape content $\mathrm{ct}$ agrees with $w$ on the interval from $-1$ through $|w|$ when read relative to head position $\mathrm{cp}$, and let $d=\operatorname{val}_2(w)$. Run the machine that repeatedly writes the pattern on tape $i$, using the binary word as its counter, for $d(|\mathrm{pat}|+1)+\mathrm{overhead}(w,d+1)$ steps from the counter-loop configuration built from $c$, $\mathrm{ct}$, and $\mathrm{cp}$. The resulting configuration is the counter-loop configuration in state done whose simulated configuration has tape $i$ patched with $d$ consecutive copies of $\mathrm{pat}$, whose head on tape $i$ has advanced by $d|\mathrm{pat}|$, and whose counter tape is true exactly on the original word interval; before that time it is in neither done nor escape. Throughout the run, the counter head stays between $\mathrm{cp}-1$ and $\mathrm{cp}+|w|$, and each simulated tape head stays between its starting position and its position advanced by $d|\mathrm{pat}|$ on tape $i$, while every other simulated tape head remains fixed.
hypotheses_covered: i is a work-tape index among k tapes
ct agrees with w on the stated interval relative to cp
d equals the binary value of w
caveat: The formal conclusion includes an exact configuration equality and bounds at every time; the prose summarizes the defined counter overhead and configuration construction.
